field.label: Enable Log Processor (IDS)
field.help: Enable/disable the CrowdSec agent. Keep this enabled to detect attacks and receive alerts from the CrowSec central service.

field.label: Enable LAPI
field.help: Enable/disable the CrowdSec Local API. Keep this enabled unless you connect to a LAPI on another machine. To connect the remediation component to a LAPI on another machine, set "Remediation component connects to" to "Remote LAPI".

field.label: Enable Remediation Component (IPS)
field.help: Enable/disable the remediation component. Keep this enabled to block packets from the attacking IP addresses.

field.label: Remediation component connects to
field.help: The LAPI that provides the decisions to block. "Local LAPI" is the LAPI running on this firewall. Choose "Remote LAPI" to block the decisions of a LAPI on another machine, for example a central CrowdSec server. The local LAPI can then be disabled, or keep serving other machines; its decisions are then not blocked by this firewall.

field.label: Remote LAPI URL
field.help: URL of the remote LAPI, for example http://192.168.1.10:8080/

field.label: Remote LAPI API key
field.help: API key of a bouncer registered on the remote LAPI. For security the stored key is never shown; leave the field empty to keep it.

field.label: Enrollment key from https://app.crowdsec.net
field.help: Click "Enroll command" on the the website and copy the key here.

field.label: Manual LAPI configuration
field.help: Avoid overwriting LAPI settings for config.yaml, local_api_credentials.yaml, crowdsec-firewall-bouncer.yaml. The next two configuration options (lapi_listen_address, lapi_listen_port) will be ignored, as well as the remote LAPI settings of the remediation component. Allows configurations not covered by these settings, like linking together multiple opnsense instances, connecting the log processor to an existing crowdsec multi-server setup, or TLS client certificates.

field.label: LAPI listen address
field.help:
Where to listen for LAPI connections: IP address. The default value is 127.0.0.1. You can change it to a LAN address to connect from other agents/machines and bouncers.
This is written in /usr/local/etc/crowdsec/config.yaml, local_api_credentials.yaml and, when the remediation component connects to the local LAPI, bouncers/crowdsec-firewall-bouncer.yaml. To enable TLS, add the certificate information to config.yaml and change http to https in the other two files. Comments in YAML will not be preserved.

field.label: LAPI listen port
field.help: Where to listen for LAPI connections: port. The default value is 8080, but you can change it to avoid conflicts with existing services.

field.label: Create blocklist rules
field.help: Generate block rules from the Crowdsec blocklists. They are applied to all interfaces, ipv4/v6, ingress and egress. If you disable this, you'll have to write your own rules to block anything.

field.label: Enable log for rules
field.help: Enable log collection for CrowdSec's block rules.

field.label: Tag for matched packets
field.help: Add a tag to packets that are dropped by CrowdSec rules for diagnostic purposes.
